title: The Holographic Principle
description: Everything inside a volume is encoded on its boundary, black holes included.

puzzle.goal: The maximum entropy that fits inside a region is set not by its volume but by the area of its boundary: one quarter of a unit of kB for every Planck area (Għ/c³) of the enclosing surface. Write the entropy of a spherical horizon of radius r by integrating the area element over the sphere.
puzzle.name: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy (area law)
puzzle.form: kB * c ^ 3 / ( 4 * G * ħ ) * int ( 0 , π , int ( 0 , 2 * π , r ^ 2 * sin ( θ ) , φ ) , θ )
puzzle.ask: The integral gives S = πkB r²/l², with l the Planck length. Find the information capacity in bits (S/(kB ln 2)) of a horizon of radius r = @{r} Planck lengths.
puzzle.method: Integrate r² sin θ over the sphere to get the area, then divide by four Planck areas (4Għ/c³) and multiply by kB.
